articles.title: Bryce James opens Arizona exhibition with a 3 as LeBron begins his 24th NBA season and their family’s next chapter takes shape
articles.standfirst: The father and son are approaching very different basketball milestones as Bryce builds his own path in college and LeBron prepares for another NBA season
articles.summary: The father and son are approaching very different basketball milestones as Bryce builds his own path in college and LeBron prepares for another NBA season
articles.body:
B ryce James made his first shot of Arizona’s exhibition against San Francisco count. The sophomore guard opened the scoring with a three-pointer on Arizona’s first possession, giving him a small but memorable moment as he continues to find his footing in college basketball. Arizona went on to win 93-69 , and Bryce finished with three points, one assist and one steal in 14 minutes.

That first basket arrived just days before his father, LeBron James, is set to begin his 24th NBA season this time with the Philadelphia 76ers . The regular season is scheduled to open Oct. 20.

Bryce is not entering his second year of high school; he is a sophomore at Arizona after redshirting last season. That extra year gave him time to develop before stepping into a college program, and one exhibition game cannot predict how far he will go. But a confident opening shot is the kind of moment that lets him show what he can do on his own court.

Bryce and Bronny are building different paths

The family’s basketball story also includes Bronny James, who is with the Los Angeles Lakers. His move into the NBA brought intense attention, with every performance measured against his famous last name and his father’s legacy.

Bryce is facing a different stage of that scrutiny: he is still developing in college, with more room to grow before professional expectations arrive.

The comparisons between the brothers are inevitable, but their careers will not follow the same timeline. LeBron’s achievements may shape how people talk about his sons, yet neither has to reproduce his career to make his own mark.

For Bryce, the next step is simply to keep learning, earn minutes and turn flashes like this opening three into steady progress.

For LeBron, the new season is another chance to compete at the highest level and make the most of his time in the league by chasing every record within reach, while his sons pursue their own basketball ambitions . For Bryce, this shot is just one step on the path he is forging in basketball, with plenty of anticipation surrounding what he might accomplish if he reaches the NBA.

articles.title: Bill Belichick's controversial dismissal of the college sport that helped UNC forge a 116-year legacy
articles.standfirst: The six-time Super Bowl champion's latest comments have raised eyebrows
articles.summary: The six-time Super Bowl champion's latest comments have raised eyebrows
articles.body:
Bill Belichick has never been known for diplomatic answers, and his remarks about basketball have sparked fresh debate about his relationship with North Carolina's celebrated sporting tradition.

During a weekly press conference, the Tar Heels football coach was asked about basketball and reportedly offered a blunt assessment: “I don't know anything about basketball. Basketball is a pretty simple game. It's putting a ball in a hoop.”

At UNC, the comment carries extra weight. The university has spent generations building a reputation as one of college basketball's most successful institutions, making Belichick's apparent dismissal notable.

The program's history stretches back to 1910, producing generations of outstanding players, iconic coaches and championship-winning teams. The men's basketball team has captured six NCAA national championships, reached a record 21 Final Fours and collected 18 ACC Tournament titles.

Its celebrated legacy includes Michael Jordan and legendary coach Dean Smith , whose influence helped establish North Carolina as a basketball powerhouse.

Belichick's remarks might sound dismissive of a sport that's central to the university's identity. However, his reputation for bluntness suggests he may simply have been expressing his focus rather than trying to insult the Tar Heels' basketball tradition.

Belichick's football rebuild faces its own test

While basketball established UNC's national reputation, football has struggled to achieve comparable championship success. The program has nevertheless produced NFL greats, including Hall of Famers Lawrence Taylor and Julius Peppers , alongside numerous memorable seasons and conference achievements.

Belichick arrived with enormous expectations after winning six Super Bowls as an NFL head coach. His first season in Chapel Hill proved difficult, with North Carolina finishing 4-8 in 2025. The disappointing campaign intensified scrutiny of the coaching change and the university's substantial investment in rebuilding its football program.

There are encouraging signs in 2026, however. North Carolina improved to 3-2 after defeating No. 25 Pittsburgh 21-17 on October 10, securing Belichick's first victory over a ranked opponent with the Tar Heels.

The result offered evidence that his team might be progressing after last season's struggles.

Belichick also praised his current players' commitment while appearing to criticize some who departed the program.

"Generally speaking, this team is more engaged," Belichick told reporters. "They work harder. They're more dedicated and they put more into it, so they get more out of it. And it's important to them. Some of the players that left here, I don't know how important things were to them."

Nevertheless, one victory doesn't erase the challenges ahead, particularly with demanding ACC matchups remaining on the schedule. Belichick will need sustained improvement to convince supporters that his approach can produce lasting results.

UNC's basketball history won't disappear as football pursues greater success. Until football begins competing for major championships consistently, basketball will remain the standard against which UNC's sporting ambitions are measured.

articles.title: College baseball player dies after being struck by a train at age 18: "We are heartbroken"
articles.standfirst: Wheaton College student dies after his car is struck by an eastbound freight train in Illinois
articles.summary: Wheaton College student dies after his car is struck by an eastbound freight train in Illinois
articles.body:
The college baseball community is mourning the tragic death of Tomassino “Tommy” Offer , an 18-year-old Wheaton College student who was killed when a freight train struck his car in Wheaton, Illinois, on Sunday, October 11.

The fatal collision occurred at approximately 10:15 a.m. near Main Street and Front Street, about 25 miles west of Chicago.

According to a Metra spokesperson, Offer had stopped at the railway crossing while a westbound freight train passed. Once it cleared the crossing, he began driving forward, but an eastbound freight train struck his vehicle.

His sudden death has devastated teammates, classmates and friends, prompting heartfelt tributes from those who knew him as a dedicated athlete and a compassionate young man.

Wheaton College baseball coach Matt Husted shared the team’s grief in a statement released through the university.

“Our team is grieving and our hearts are heavy as we grieve alongside Tommy’s family and friends,” Husted said.

He described Offer as sincere, joyful and fiercely competitive, qualities that made him a valued member of the baseball team. The coach also highlighted the teenager’s ability to make others feel appreciated, explaining that he developed meaningful relationships throughout the college community.

Friends and schools unite to honor teen’s memory

According to ABC Eyewitness News, Offer was originally from Michigan and had attended church on the morning of the collision. Reverend Santos Castillo of St. Michael Catholic Church recalled seeing the teenager shortly before he left for Chicago with a friend.

Castillo remembered Offer waving goodbye, reflecting on how an ordinary farewell had become their final encounter.

“I definitely saw him before he left, and he just waved at me, and together with his friend Joe, they were here together, and who would have known that was the last time he’d be in church,” Castillo said.

Students from Wheaton College and the surrounding community gathered on Monday to pay tribute to Offer . The university also held a separate memorial on Sunday evening, allowing students and friends to come together and support one another during an incredibly difficult time.

Notre Dame Preparatory School in Pontiac, Michigan, where Offer previously studied, also released a statement remembering its former student.

“ Tomassino Offer was an outstanding student and an even better young man,” the school said, highlighting the affection he received from teachers and classmates.

Offer had built friendships through both baseball and soccer. His former school also celebrated his sporting achievements, including being part of a soccer team that won a state championship.

His influence extended across classrooms, sports teams, church and college life, leaving behind a wide network of people now struggling to come to terms with his death.

At just 18, Offer had a future filled with possibilities, making the loss particularly painful for his family, friends and teammates.

Authorities are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the collision.

articles.title: The shocking confession of Karrueche Tran, Deion Sanders' girlfriend: "I would be embarrassed"
articles.standfirst: Karrueche Tran explains why Deion Sanders’ confidence after losing two toes impresses her
articles.summary: Karrueche Tran explains why Deion Sanders’ confidence after losing two toes impresses her
articles.body:
Karrueche Tran has opened up about her relationship with Deion Sanders , revealing why she admires the Colorado football coach’s confidence following the loss of two toes.

During an appearance on The Pop Exchange Show on October 15, Tran admitted that she might struggle with the same situation, but Sanders hasn’t allowed his medical challenges to change his personality or outlook on life.

“I would be embarrassed or feel not confident with having just three toes,” Tran confessed, acknowledging how difficult it could be for someone to adjust to such a significant physical change.

However, she praised Sanders for speaking openly about his experience instead of hiding it from others.

“He [Deion] didn’t allow this to bring him down or completely change who he is,” said Karrueche .

“I really truly commend him for that and for being vocal about it, too. I can imagine somebody or anybody; I would be embarrassed or feel not confident with having just three toes.”

Her comments followed a photo she shared showing the couple displaying his feet and newly fitted prosthetic toes.

Sanders ’ medical problems began in September 2021, when he underwent surgery for a dislocated toe and an inflamed nerve. Complications involving blood clots and restricted circulation subsequently threatened his leg.

Doctors performed multiple procedures, eventually removing his left big toe and second toe in 2022. Amputation below the knee was also considered.

The ordeal kept Sanders in hospital for approximately a month, even as he remained connected to his coaching responsibilities at Jackson State. Tran recalled the severity of the situation, explaining that his toes had turned black. Their loss also affected his balance, forcing him to adjust how he walked.

Prosthetic toes bring a fresh reason to laugh

Sanders received custom-made prosthetic toes in September 2026, marking another milestone in his recovery. His son, Deion Sanders Jr ., shared footage of the moment on September 16, giving fans a look at the new additions.

The coach welcomed the change with humor, announcing that he was “10 toes down again!” He also described the prosthetics as a blessing and joked that they would help him fill his shoes properly and return to wearing his usual size 11.5 footwear.

Tran has been impressed by how realistic the replacements look, including their carefully designed toenails. However, Sanders still needs time to adjust. His remaining toes have reportedly curved from gripping the ground, while the prosthetics sit straighter, creating a difference he must accommodate when walking.

Humor has become an important part of how the couple handles the experience. Tran affectionately calls his foot “Little Foot” and regularly teases him about it. She explained that being able to laugh together has become a positive part of their relationship.

She also recalled the first time she noticed his foot while visiting his home. Sanders was lying in bed watching television, with his foot propped up and his toes visible. Having never discussed the subject before, Tran didn’t know how to approach it.

“He obviously doesn’t care,” she said of that instance. “He’s not embarrassed.”

articles.title: Tyler Ulrich cause of death: The college player dies at 21 after a serious injury during a game
articles.standfirst: The Southern Nazarene University safety died five days after suffering a traumatic injury on the field
articles.summary: The Southern Nazarene University safety died five days after suffering a traumatic injury on the field
articles.body:
T yler Ulrich , a 21-year-old college football player at Southern Nazarene University (SNU) , has died after suffering a serious injury during a game in Arkansas.

The sophomore safety passed away on Thursday, October 15, five days after the incident that left him hospitalized and prompted an outpouring of support from his family, teammates and wider university community.

Ulrich’s official cause of death has not been disclosed. Southern Nazarene confirmed that he suffered what it described as a “traumatic injury” during its game against Ouachita Baptist University on Saturday, October 10.

Reports identified the injury as a head injury, but the university has not publicly provided further medical details or explained the precise circumstances that led to his death.

The incident occurred during a Division II matchup in Arkadelphia, Arkansas. Play was stopped for nearly an hour as medical personnel treated Ulrich on the field. He was subsequently taken to a hospital, where he remained for five days before his death was announced.

The circumstances have brought renewed attention to the dangers of serious injuries in American football. However, without an official medical explanation, it would be premature to draw conclusions about the specific injury or the events that caused Ulrich’s death.

SNU Athletics shared the news on social media, writing: “It is with heavy hearts that we share the loss of our SNU football player, Tyler Ulrich ,” before expressing its condolences to those affected by the tragedy.

“This loss is deeply felt across our campus. Our hearts are with his family, friends, teammates, and everyone who knew him. We ask that you join us in lifting them up in prayer.”

Tyler Ulrich remembered by his family and football community

The reaction to Ulrich’s death has reflected the impact he made beyond the football field. Southern Nazarene head coach Dustin Hada paid tribute to the player’s character in a social media post, describing the qualities he believed defined him.

“Man of God, ultimate example of quiet strength, loyal, worker, joyous. That’s who Tyler was!!”

Ulrich’s father, Mark, had also been sharing updates as the family waited for news about his son’s condition. In a Facebook post earlier on Thursday, he thanked those who had offered prayers and support while explaining how desperately the family hoped for a recovery.

“Our family is truly blessed to receive all the love and prayers for our young Tyler and we are ever grateful,” he wrote. “But as much support and love that was given, it is with a heavy heart I am writing to say the Lord called Tyler this morning at 11:13 a.m.”

The message marked the end of a painful period of uncertainty for those closest to Ulrich . Although the family had received widespread encouragement, he ultimately did not recover from the injury.

Originally from Azle, Texas, Ulrich was in his third season with Southern Nazarene, a university based in Bethany, Oklahoma. He had started 16 of his 20 appearances for the programme, including six games during the current season, and recorded 36 tackles.

His role as a safety involved helping defend against opposing passing and running plays, making him an important part of the team's defensive unit.

The university also confirmed that its scheduled game against Southwestern Oklahoma State University on Saturday, October 17, would not take place.

Southwestern Oklahoma State announced the cancellation, offering its support to the SNU programme and university community as they mourned Ulrich.

For now, the precise medical cause of Ulrich’s death remains unconfirmed publicly. What is clear is that a young athlete’s life ended following an on-field emergency, leaving his family, friends and teammates to grieve a loss that came only days after the game.
